sectionsUsed: Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap, release table: Java SE 25 is a long-term support (LTS) release, the most recent LTS.
OpenJDK JDK 25 project page, Status and Schedule: JDK 25 reached General Availability; the page lists its features.
JDK 25 Installation Guide, Overview of JDK Installation: the JDK is installed per operating system (macOS, Linux, Windows); the guide links the per-platform steps.

Eclipse Temurin releases page: pick a version (JDK 25 - LTS listed), package type (JDK or JRE) and platform, then download; the course links it as the place to choose system, architecture, JDK 25 and the JDK package type. A JRE is still offered here, so the page tells learners to pick JDK.
Adoptium macOS PKG installer packages, GUI installation: download the .pkg, open it, Continue, accept the license, Install. The page links this as the official macOS JDK guide.

Adoptium Linux (RPM/DEB/APK) installer packages: configure the Adoptium repository for apt, dnf/yum, zypper or apk, then install the temurin-<version>-jdk package, e.g. temurin-25-jdk. The page links this as the official Linux JDK guide.

Adoptium Windows MSI installer packages, GUI installation: open the .msi, accept the license; the feature that updates the PATH environment variable is a default, and the feature that updates JAVA_HOME can be selected; Install. The page links this as the official Windows JDK guide. Note: Windows installer packages are supported only on Windows x64 systems, so the page tells ARM-based Windows learners to ask their instructor.

Dev.java, Getting Started with Java, sections on the JDK and the JRE: the JDK holds javac and java; the JRE is a subset that only ran applications and is no longer distributed by OpenJDK or Oracle; set up PATH so the JDK tools are found.

Apache Maven, Installing Apache Maven, Prerequisites and Binary distribution: a JDK is needed, found via JAVA_HOME or the java executable on PATH; download the binary archive, extract it and add its bin directory to PATH; confirm with mvn -v in a new shell, which also prints the Java version Maven uses. JAVA_HOME priority over PATH also read from the bin/mvn launcher script of Apache Maven 3.9.16.

Apache Maven, Download page: Maven 3.10.0 is the latest release and 3.9.x is still maintained; both require JDK 8 or above to run; binary tar.gz and zip archives for all platforms. Supports the expected mvn -v output Apache Maven 3.9 or later.
IntelliJ IDEA help, Install IntelliJ IDEA: installation on macOS, Linux and Windows. The page links this as the official IDE install guide.
IntelliJ IDEA help, Maven, open an existing Maven project: open the pom.xml file and choose Open as Project so the IDE imports the Maven project.

IntelliJ IDEA help, SDKs, Add a project SDK: File | Project Structure | Project Settings | Project, select the SDK, or Add JDK from disk with its home directory, or Download JDK; the IDE keeps its own list of JDKs, separate from the terminal PATH.
Dev.java, Building a Java application in IntelliJ IDEA: creating or opening a project and choosing its JDK.
Dev.java, Building a Java application in Visual Studio Code: the documented alternative IDE.
Apple Support, Mac computers with Apple silicon: on a Mac with Apple silicon, About This Mac (Apple menu) shows Chip; on an Intel-based Mac it shows Processor.
Microsoft Support, 32-bit and 64-bit Windows FAQ: Start, Settings > System > About; the architecture is shown next to System type under Device specifications.

uname(1) manual page, OPTIONS: -m, --machine prints the machine hardware name. The specific x86_64 and aarch64 values named on the page are not printed in this manual and are listed as unverified in topic.json freshness.
